declarations.en: An elementary map is either a Möbius map $h(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)$ with $a,b,c,d∈ℚ$ and $ad-bc≠0$, or a polynomial $p∈ℚ[X]$ with $\deg p>0$. On $ℚ̄∪{∞}$ a Möbius map sends a finite denominator-zero point to $∞$, and sends $∞$ to $∞$ if $c=0$ and to $a/c$ otherwise; a polynomial sends $∞$ to $∞$. Its index $r_h(z)$ is $1$ for a Möbius map; for a polynomial it is $\deg p$ at $∞$, and the multiplicity of $z$ as a root of $p(X)-p(z)$ after extending coefficients to $ℚ̄$ at finite $z$. For a finite list $H=(h_1,…,h_k)$, let $F_H=h_k∘⋯∘h_1$ on these points, and let $R_H(z)$ be the product of the successive indices along this orbit. The empty list gives $F_H(z)=z$ and $R_H(z)=1$. This defines the point action $h(z)$ specified above, for every elementary-map datum $h$ and every finite or infinite point $z$. The algebraic numbers are elements of the fixed algebraic closure of $ℚ$.
declarations.zh_Hans: 初等映射指以下两类之一：Möbius 映射 $h(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)$，其中 $a,b,c,d∈ℚ$ 且 $ad-bc≠0$；或正次数多项式 $p∈ℚ[X]$。在 $ℚ̄∪{∞}$ 上，Möbius 映射把有限的分母为零点映到 $∞$，把 $∞$ 在 $c=0$ 时映到 $∞$、在 $c≠0$ 时映到 $a/c$；多项式把 $∞$ 映到 $∞$。其指数 $r_h(z)$ 对 Möbius 映射恒为 $1$；对多项式，在 $∞$ 处为 $\deg p$，在有限 $z$ 处为扩充系数到 $ℚ̄$ 后 $z$ 作为 $p(X)-p(z)$ 的根的重数。对有限列表 $H=(h_1,…,h_k)$，令 $F_H=h_k∘⋯∘h_1$ 为点上的复合，$R_H(z)$ 为沿相继像点的这些指数之积。空列表给出 $F_H(z)=z$、$R_H(z)=1$。 此处对每个初等映射数据 $h$ 及每个有限或无穷远点 $z$，定义上述点作用 $h(z)$；代数数取自固定的 $ℚ$ 的代数闭包。

declarations.en: Let $K$ be any field of characteristic zero. For an elementary datum consisting of $a,b,c,d∈ℚ$ with $ad-bc≠0$, and any $f∈K$, this defines $(af+b)/(cf+d)$ in $K$; for an elementary datum $p∈ℚ[X]$ of strictly positive natural degree, it defines $p(f)$. Rational numbers are mapped into $K$ by its canonical embedding. This is a total $K$-valued operation: a zero denominator gives zero.

declarations.ja: $K$ を任意の標数零の体とする。 初等データ $a,b,c,d∈ℚ$、$ad-bc≠0$ と任意の $f∈K$ に対して、$K$ 内の $(af+b)/(cf+d)$ を定める。自然次数が正の初等多項式データ $p∈ℚ[X]$ に対しては $p(f)$ とする。有理数は標準埋め込みで $K$ に写す。これは $K$ 値の全域演算であり、分母が零なら値は零である。

declarations.en: An elementary map is either a Möbius map $h(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)$ with $a,b,c,d∈ℚ$ and $ad-bc≠0$, or a polynomial $p∈ℚ[X]$ with $\deg p>0$. On $ℚ̄∪{∞}$ a Möbius map sends a finite denominator-zero point to $∞$, and sends $∞$ to $∞$ if $c=0$ and to $a/c$ otherwise; a polynomial sends $∞$ to $∞$. Its index $r_h(z)$ is $1$ for a Möbius map; for a polynomial it is $\deg p$ at $∞$, and the multiplicity of $z$ as a root of $p(X)-p(z)$ after extending coefficients to $ℚ̄$ at finite $z$. For a finite list $H=(h_1,…,h_k)$, let $F_H=h_k∘⋯∘h_1$ on these points, and let $R_H(z)$ be the product of the successive indices along this orbit. The empty list gives $F_H(z)=z$ and $R_H(z)=1$. Let $ℚ̄$ be the fixed algebraic closure of $ℚ$. For every finite set $S⊆ℚ̄∪{∞}$, assume that for every $ℚ$-algebra automorphism $σ$ of $ℚ̄$ and every $z∈S$, the point obtained by applying $σ$ to finite $z$ and fixing $∞$ also belongs to $S$, and assume $0∉S$. Then there exists a finite list $H$ of the specified elementary maps such that every $z∈S$ has $F_H(z)∈{∞,0,1}$, $F_H(0)∉{∞,0,1}$, and every $z∈ℚ̄∪{∞}$ with $R_H(z)>1$ has $F_H(z)∈{∞,0,1}$. The set $S$ may be empty; no nonemptiness condition is placed on the witnessing list.

declarations.en: Let $N$ be a natural number and let $M$ consist of an intermediate field $K$ between $ℚ$ and an algebraic closure of $ℚ(t)$, and elements $u,v∈K$, such that $u$ is transcendental over $ℚ$ (no nonzero polynomial over $ℚ$ vanishes at $u$), $u^N+v^N=1$, the subfield generated by $ℚ,u,v$ is $K$, and $K$ is finite dimensional over the subfield $ℚ(u)$ with dimension exactly $N$. There is no separate restriction on $N$; the assertion concerns supplied data satisfying all these conditions. For $N=0$ the equation would be $1+1=1$ in characteristic zero, so no such model is supplied and assertions conditional on it are vacuous. A place $P$ means a valuation subring $O_P⊊K$ containing every rational number; $κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P$ is its residue field. Assume $h_{DVR}$: every such $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring. Write $v_P(f)$ for minus the integer logarithm of its maximal-ideal valuation at $f$, the normalized integer order with the total-function convention $v_P(0)=0$. For $f∈K$, define $e_f(P)$ as follows: if $f∈O_P$, let $m_{P,f}$ be the minimal polynomial over $ℚ$ of its residue in $κ(P)$ and put $e_f(P)=v_P(m_{P,f}(f))$; if $f∉O_P$, put $e_f(P)=-v_P(f)$. Define $C_f={P:v_P(f)≠0\text{ or }v_P(f-1)>0}$. Assume additionally $h_{RF}$: each residue field $κ(P)$ is finite dimensional over $ℚ$. For every $φ∈K$, assume $φ$ is transcendental over $ℚ$ and that for every place $P$, $e_φ(P)>1$ implies $P∈C_φ$; this conjunction is the stated Belyi hypothesis. Then $C_φ$ is finite.
